scope.ghidra_mode: explicit-program observation only; no implementation, no project save, no re-analysis, no historical edits

question: Is the anonymous 24-slot record produced by 0x00e39ab0 a companion/view of the anonymous 27-slot record, a separate event, or an independent keyed entry; and what are the exact ownership, consumer, serialization, protocol, and release boundaries?

verdict.primary_27: A 27-slot raw 32-bit value stored under key 0x0c in the keyed container embedded in the DAT_015fd910 owner.
verdict.secondary_24: A separate 24-slot raw 32-bit value stored under key 0x06 in the same owner. It is not an alias or pointer view of key 0x0c.
verdict.relation: The two values are construction-coupled companion/sidecar records in the anonymous space/telemetry builder family, but they are independent physical table entries. The 24-slot value is not established as a separately dispatched event.
verdict.architecture_boundary: Keep two opaque independent entries with an explicit producer-side association. Do not model either as a universal event, cCommEvent, App message, UTFWin message, animation record, or wire protocol record.
verdict.smallest_blocker: No static caller was found that reads key 0x06, and no runtime instance was captured that relates the key-0x06 value to the key-0x0c value. This is the only remaining separator capable of changing the minimum semantic model.
verdict.redesign_force: Not forced by current evidence. A direct key-0x06 consumer, dispatch, or runtime alias could force redesign; absent that separator, two opaque entries are the safe minimum.

exact_observation.target_prologue: 0x00e39ab0 resolves DAT_015fd910 through FUN_0067de90, creates the key-0x0c value, resizes it to 0x1b slots, populates it, creates the key-0x06 value, resizes it to 0x18 slots, populates it, and returns only the key-0x0c handle.
primary_construction: FUN_007ec160 is called with ECX=owner and key argument 0x0c, value argument 0.
FUN_007eb820 is called on the returned value with count 0x1b.
The returned handle exposes a payload pointer at handle+0x0c; the payload contains 27 consecutive 32-bit slots.
The function writes the discriminator, zero, timestamp-like value, two supplied/derived triples, object IDs, lookup values, the raw constant 0x053DBCF2, and caller-supplied tuples/scalars.
secondary_construction: FUN_007ec160 is called again with ECX=owner and key argument 0x06, value argument 0.
FUN_007eb820 is called on the second returned value with count 0x18.
The second handle exposes a separate payload pointer at handle+0x0c; the payload contains 24 consecutive 32-bit slots.
The second handle remains in EDI/local state and is not returned or passed to a later function after its field writes.

constant_correction.use: written to the primary lookup/sentinel slot when the optional lookup is absent; the same semantic use is visible in sibling builders where applicable

exact_observation.no_alias_observation: There is no assignment of the primary payload pointer, primary handle, or key-0x0c node into the key-0x06 value, and no reverse assignment. The two vectors have different lengths and separate allocation/value nodes.

owner_and_constructor_trace.global_installer: 0x0067e0b0 stores the owner pointer into DAT_015fd910.

observations: Installs the owner vtable and secondary interface vtable.
Sets the embedded keyed-container bucket pointer at owner+0x10 and bucket count at owner+0x14.
Sets owner+0x18 to zero and initializes telemetry-related fields at owner+0x30, owner+0x34, owner+0x38, and owner+0x3c.
FUN_007e67a0 invokes the owner vtable slot at +0x04 after construction.
FUN_007ebf40 clears the embedded bucket table through FUN_007eb950, resets owner+0x18, and initializes owner+0x30/+0x34 through FUN_0092e3d0(2).
Uses the owner as this and the first argument as the key.
Calls the embedded bucket lookup/insert machinery through FUN_007ebfd0.
Returns a value handle whose +0x0c field points at the raw slot payload.
Uses the requested count to prepare the 4-byte slot storage.
For the target it is invoked with 0x1b for key 0x0c and 0x18 for key 0x06.
The value is raw storage, not a vtable-bearing record object.

pair_hypotheses.name: pointer_view_or_alias
pair_hypotheses.statement: The 24-slot record is a view, alias, or projection over the same 27-slot object.
predictions: Both records would share a payload pointer, node, or allocator identity.
Writing one record would be observable through the other without a keyed lookup.
One record would be returned and the other would not require a separate key/value insertion.
evidence_for: Both are created in one builder and use the same discriminator and timestamp/lookup sources.
Both are written with related position, object-ID, and scalar values.
evidence_against: The target inserts key 0x0c and key 0x06 through two distinct FUN_007ec160 calls.
The two records have distinct slot counts, 0x1b versus 0x18, and distinct value handles.
The key-0x06 handle is local and is not returned; no pointer field connects it to key 0x0c.
The key-0x0c value is read by the consumer family, while the caller census contains no key-0x06 lookup.

pair_hypotheses.name: separate_event
pair_hypotheses.statement: The 24-slot record is an independent event with its own dispatch, consumer, and lifetime.
predictions: It would be returned or passed to a distinct consumer.
It would have a distinct dispatch token or table-iteration path.
It would have an independent creation and release contract rather than a producer-side side effect.
evidence_for: It has its own key, value node, and 24-slot storage.
The common telemetry serializer can serialize a selected key independently, so it is not required to be an alias.
evidence_against: All observed key-0x06 creation sites also create key 0x0c in the same builder and mirror common input sources.
The 24-slot handle is never returned from FUN_00e39ab0 or its sibling builders.
No direct key-0x06 consumer, dispatch call, queue insertion, or independent release site was found.
Its construction is a side effect of the key-0x0c builder rather than an independently scheduled producer.

pair_hypotheses.name: independent_entry_with_producer_coupled_companion_semantics
pair_hypotheses.statement: The 24-slot value is an independent keyed entry whose semantic relationship to the 27-slot value is limited to coupled construction and common field provenance.
predictions: The two values should have different keys, sizes, and value nodes.
The producer should populate both from the same discriminator, timestamp, object, position, and caller inputs.
The key-0x0c value should have consumers; the key-0x06 value may be dormant or consumed by an undiscovered path.
The common table owner should serialize or release both through generic keyed-container infrastructure.
evidence_for: 0x00e39ab0 and sibling builders 0x00e394f0, 0x00e39710, 0x00e398e0, and 0x00e3c7c0 repeat the 0x0c/27 plus 0x06/24 construction pattern.
The repeated builders call the same initializer and lookup helpers and mirror related fields into both arrays.
The key-0x0c value is enumerated and updated by the space-state consumer family.
Generic owner teardown and telemetry serialization operate on keyed values rather than on a shared record object.
evidence_against: The static graph cannot prove that the sidecar has no semantic purpose in a runtime-only consumer.
No positive key-0x06 read or runtime instance correlation is available.

pair_hypotheses.name: cCommEvent_or_universal_event_family
pair_hypotheses.statement: The pair is a cCommEvent variant or one universal event payload shared with App, UI, animation, and command families.
predictions: A cCommEvent constructor, ISimulatorSerializable vtable, manager insertion, and refcount path would be reached from the pair.
The payload would expose cCommEvent's 0xa0 layout rather than separate raw vectors.
A message-manager, UI window, animation, or command/protocol dispatch edge would carry the record.
evidence_for: 0x0102d1b0 and 0x0102df20 co-call the target and the cCommManager space-event creation path, and the surrounding subsystem is space/trade oriented.
evidence_against: Ghidra's cCommEvent layout is 0xa0 bytes with two vtable pointers, mnRefCount, intrusive pointers, and four vectors.
FUN_00aeb160 allocates 0xa0, constructs a cCommEvent, inserts it into a manager vector, and performs virtual AddRef/Release operations; the target constructs raw 27/24 slot values instead.
The target's direct path has no cCommEvent constructor, manager insertion, record vtable, refcount, or serializer object edge.
The consumer path uses raw slot offsets and keyed state-table dispatch, not App/UTFWin/animation/command transport.

pair_hypotheses.name: command_or_network_protocol_record
pair_hypotheses.statement: The 27/24 values are command-line, network, or resource protocol records.
predictions: A parser, command grammar, Resource::IRecord, IStream codec, network framing, or protocol dispatch would be directly connected.
The record would have encoded command/resource fields or a protocol owner rather than generic keyed slot storage.
evidence_for: The first slot is a numeric discriminator and the arrays contain IDs, positions, and scalars, which is structurally compatible with a tagged record in principle.
evidence_against: The direct target/consumer path contains no CommandLine, pdtk, Resource::IRecord, network, or protocol parser/codec edge.
The only positive serialization path found is the generic App/Telemetry MemoryStream path, not a game protocol or resource record.
Ownership is the DAT_015fd910 keyed owner and its generic bucket release helpers.

consumer_families.role: Looks up or iterates key 0x0c, then reads the 27-slot values through list/value handles. These are the primary observed consumers.
consumer_families.key_0x06_observation: No direct key-0x06 lookup appears in the callers of FUN_007eb100. The generic FUN_00668c80 caller receives keys 7, 8, 9, 10, or 11 from FUN_00668d90, not 6.

consumer_families.role: FUN_00e3a270 switches on a 32-bit token and copies record slots into a space-state object. It is called from the key-0x0c orchestration path, not from a key-0x06-specific dispatcher.

FUN_00e39420 reads a triple at a slot index; FUN_00e393e0 writes a triple; FUN_00e39de0 compares and updates two triples; FUN_00e39450 fills the sidecar's lookup-derived triples. The first three are observed in the 27-slot consumer path; FUN_00e39450 is observed in the builders.

These downstream functions consume slots or values derived from the key-0x0c record and perform property, resource-key, UI, or placement work. They do not establish that the carrier itself is a UI, resource, or Cell record.
These callers co-produce the anonymous pair and a cCommManager space communication event. The co-call is correlation only; no pointer or slot dataflow joins the two objects.
No direct consumer was recovered. The absence is a static caller-census result, not proof that no indirect/runtime consumer exists.

ownership_and_release.owner: DAT_015fd910 owner, installed by FUN_0067e0b0 and initialized by FUN_007ec0a0 plus virtual initialization at 0x007ebf40.
ownership_and_release.embedded_container: The owner contains the keyed bucket structure used by FUN_007ec160; the values own the 27/24 slot buffers.
generic_release: FUN_007eb950 walks all buckets and frees payload nodes and their attached buffers.
FUN_007eb9e0 removes every matching key entry and frees the value nodes.
FUN_007ebb60 selects all-entry clearing for key -1 or one-key removal for another argument.
FUN_007ebe70 and the owner destructor path clear the embedded container.
FUN_00e3c760 explicitly removes the key-0x0c value; no equivalent key-0x06-specific teardown was found.
ownership_and_release.record_local_ownership: The 27/24 raw slot values have no record-local vtable, AddRef, Release, or refcount path. The table owner is the observed storage/lifetime boundary.
ownership_and_release.runtime_order: Static construction order is primary insertion/initialization, primary writes, secondary insertion/initialization, secondary writes, then return of the primary handle. Exact interleaving with other producers and consumers is not runtime-observed.

positive_edge.trigger: FUN_007ec160 checks FUN_007eb090() * 0x20 against 0x2800. A count above 640 invokes FUN_007ebce0 with the current key before the keyed insertion continues.
positive_edge.payload: FUN_007ebba0 walks entries for the selected key, writes 8-byte metadata, the key, a 4-byte entry identifier, and the raw 4-byte slot array. FUN_0093aa70 byte-swaps each 32-bit value before writing.
positive_edge.destination: FUN_007ebce0 creates a MemoryStream named App/Telemetry. FUN_007eb600 may write telemetry.dat when the owner telemetry flag at owner+0x38 is enabled.
positive_edge.default_flag: FUN_007ec0a0 initializes owner+0x38 to zero, so file output is not enabled by the observed default constructor. The stream/serialization call itself remains conditional and reachable.
positive_edge.cleanup: After serializing the selected key, FUN_007ebba0 calls FUN_007eb9e0 for that key, so the selected value is removed after the telemetry dump path.

serialization.interpretation: This is a direct generic App/Telemetry encoding edge for the table values, including either 27/24 key when that key is selected. It is not evidence of game save persistence, resource serialization, network protocol framing, or a read-back ABI.
negative_edges: No direct cGamePersistenceManager, ClassSerializer, ISerializer, Resource::IRecord, command parser, or network codec edge was found in the target/consumer/release path.
No read-back path corresponding to the App/Telemetry dump was found in the focused census.

evidence: The target uses generic keyed insertion and raw slot writes.
The positive byte-writing helpers are reached through the App/Telemetry MemoryStream path and are not a command or network parser.
The observed consumer families are keyed state enumeration, numeric dispatch, raw slot access, and downstream property/presentation work.
protocol_boundary.prediction_if_protocol_were_true: A direct parser/codec or protocol owner would need to read key 0x06 or a shared pair instance. No such static edge is present.

exact_predictions.prediction: The 27-slot and 24-slot values will have different keyed-container keys, value nodes, payload pointers, and lengths.
exact_predictions.evidence: 0x00e39ab0 and four sibling builders call FUN_007ec160 with 0x0c and 0x06, then FUN_007eb820 with 0x1b and 0x18.

exact_predictions.prediction: The 24-slot value will not be a pointer alias or returned primary handle.
exact_predictions.evidence: The second handle is local, is not returned, and no cross-pointer assignment is present.

exact_predictions.prediction: The 27-slot value will be the one consumed by the observed space-state families.
exact_predictions.evidence: FUN_007eb100 callers use key 0x0c and then invoke raw-slot/state-dispatch consumers.

exact_predictions.prediction: The 24-slot value will be dormant, a producer-side sidecar, or consumed by an undiscovered indirect path.
exact_predictions.evidence: No static key-0x06 reader was found, but no runtime instance trace was performed.

exact_predictions.prediction: When the keyed container exceeds 640 entries during insertion, the selected key's value is serialized through App/Telemetry and then removed.
exact_predictions.evidence: FUN_007ec160 threshold, FUN_007ebce0, FUN_007ebba0, FUN_0093aa70, and FUN_007eb9e0 form the path.

blockers.blocker: No direct consumer or runtime instance was found for key 0x06, so the semantic role of the 24-slot sidecar remains unresolved.
blockers.smallest_next_observation: Trace one key-0x06 insertion through the later table lookup/dispatch/release path and record owner, key, value node, payload pointer, and any consumer call.
blockers.can_force_semantic_redesign: Yes, if the trace shows a distinct dispatch, protocol, or alias relationship. Current static evidence does not force redesign.

blockers.blocker: The owner class/name of DAT_015fd910 and the exact meaning of the two keyed values are not recovered.
blockers.smallest_next_observation: Recover a concrete owner/vtable identity or a direct cross-key consumer; do not infer a semantic field schema from the repeated slot counts.
blockers.can_force_semantic_redesign: Only if the recovered identity connects the value to a different established family; it is not required for the current opaque two-entry boundary.

blockers.blocker: Telemetry serialization is conditional and has no recovered read-back path.
blockers.smallest_next_observation: Observe the threshold trigger and correlate the serialized key/vector with a later reconstruction or consumer path.
blockers.can_force_semantic_redesign: Yes, if the telemetry format is an externally required ABI; it does not force a game-persistence ABI now.

freeze: 0x00e39ab0 creates key-0x0c/27-slot and key-0x06/24-slot values through separate FUN_007ec160/FUN_007eb820 calls.
The 24-slot value is not a pointer view of the 27-slot value.
The 24-slot value is producer-coupled but not established as a separate event.
The key-0x0c value has the observed raw-slot and numeric-dispatch consumer families.
DAT_015fd910 is the observed owner; generic keyed-container helpers release its values.
A conditional App/Telemetry serialization path exists and is distinct from protocol/persistence semantics.
The raw missing-lookup constant is 0x053DBCF2 (87932146), not -10.
defer: Whether key 0x06 is a dormant legacy sidecar, a companion representation consumed indirectly, or a separately meaningful event.
Exact semantic names and types for the raw slots.
Whether telemetry has a read-back or external consumer contract.
Any indirect command, resource, network, or persistence bridge.

limitations: No runtime trace was performed; exact instance identity, runtime order, and key-0x06 consumer behavior remain unknown.
Negative caller evidence is bounded to the focused static graph and does not exclude indirect dispatch.
The App/Telemetry path is a real conditional encoding edge, but its external compatibility significance is not established.
No SPORE/ traversal, no knowledgegraph/spore.db access, no implementation, and no historical file edits were performed.
